Interface ChaosDiagnostics

public interface ChaosDiagnostics
Read-only runtime view of all registered chaos scenarios and agent health.

Obtained via ChaosControlPlane.diagnostics(). The same instance is also exposed over JMX at com.macstab.chaos.jvm:type=ChaosDiagnostics and drives JFR periodic snapshot events (registered by the bootstrap module when JFR is available).

All methods return immutable point-in-time views. Counters continue to increment after the snapshot is taken.

Primary operations:

  • snapshot() — full picture: all scenarios, failures, runtime capabilities
  • scenario(String) — single-scenario lookup by ID
  • debugDump() — human-readable text suitable for logging or test failure messages

  • Method Details

    • snapshot

      ChaosDiagnostics.Snapshot snapshot()
      Returns an immutable snapshot of the full agent state at this instant.

      The snapshot includes:

      • one ChaosDiagnostics.ScenarioReport per registered scenario with current counters and state
      • the 256 most recent ChaosDiagnostics.ActivationFailure records (older ones are counted in the runtime detail droppedActivationFailures)
      • runtime details: JDK version, virtual thread support, JFR availability, dropped counts and hook health
      Returns:
      the current diagnostics snapshot

    • scenario

      Optional<ChaosDiagnostics.ScenarioReport> scenario(String scenarioId)
      Returns the current report for the scenario with the given ID, or empty if no scenario with that ID is registered. When the ID is registered in several scopes, the JVM scope's report is returned, else the report of the session with the smallest id, whichever thread asks; a session's own scenario is reported by its activation handle.
      Parameters:
      scenarioId - the scenario ID as provided to ChaosScenario.Builder.build()
      Returns:
      the scenario report, or empty if not found

    • debugDump

      String debugDump()
      Returns a multi-line human-readable diagnostics dump. Includes all scenario states, counters, failure records, and runtime capability details.

      Use in test failure messages or agent startup logging (ChaosPlan.Observability.debugDumpOnStart()).

      Returns:
      a formatted multi-line diagnostics string
